text: An AWS account is the fundamental container in AWS — it holds your resources, your billing, and every identity that can act inside it, starting with one all-powerful root user.

The root user is tied to the sign-up email and can do literally anything, including closing the account, so AWS's guidance is to lock it away behind MFA and use individual IAM users or roles for everyday access.

Real organizations rarely stop at one account — separate accounts give a hard security and billing boundary. AWS Organizations groups accounts into OUs and adds consolidated billing plus Service Control Policies as guardrails.
A mistake in "dev" can't reach "production" when they're entirely different accounts. Next up: the shared responsibility model.
